t.1.32.1: Having heard those words of the wise Kuśanābha, the hundred maidens touched his feet with their heads and spoke.
t.1.32.2: O king, Vāyu, who pervades all things, wishes to violate us; having taken to an inauspicious path, he pays no regard to dharma.
t.1.32.3: We have a father living, blessings be upon you; we are not free to act by our own will. Ask our father for us, if he will give us to you.
t.1.32.4: As we were all speaking thus, we were violently struck down by Vāyu, who was bent on wickedness and would not heed our words.
t.1.32.5: Hearing those words of theirs, the king, supremely righteous and of great splendor, replied to the hundred matchless maidens.
t.1.32.6: Daughters, you have shown the forbearance of the forbearing, and a very great duty has been fulfilled. By coming to one mind among yourselves, you have also had regard for my family.
t.1.32.7: Forbearance is indeed the ornament of women, and of a man as well; and you have shown that difficult forbearance, especially toward the gods.
t.1.32.8: Daughters, such is the forbearance found in all of you alike. Forbearance is giving, forbearance is sacrifice, and forbearance is truth, my dear daughters.
t.1.32.9: Forbearance is glory, forbearance is dharma, and on forbearance the world rests. Then, O Kākutstha, having dismissed the maidens, the king, whose valor equaled that of the gods...
t.1.32.11: At that very time, a great sage named Cūlī, celibate and of virtuous conduct, had undertaken the austerity of Brahman.
t.1.32.10: He who knew counsel deliberated with his ministers about the giving away, about the bestowal at a place and a time fitting for such a gift.
t.1.32.12: While that sage was practising austerities there, a Gandharvī named Somadā, the daughter of Ūrmilā, then attended upon him. May good fortune be with you!
t.1.32.13: And she, most steadfast in dharma, bowing low before him and wholly devoted to his service, dwelt there for a time, and the guru became pleased with her.
t.1.32.14: And in the course of time he said to her, O Raghunandana: “I am well pleased; may good fortune be yours! What favour shall I do for you?”
t.1.32.15: Knowing that the sage was fully satisfied, the gandharvī, supremely delighted and skilled in speech, spoke in a sweet voice to him who was a master of words.
t.1.32.16: Endowed with the splendor of Brahman, one who has become Brahman, you are a man of great austerity; I desire a righteous son endowed with Brahmic austerity.
t.1.32.18: Pleased with her, the brahmarṣi gave her a peerless son, a mind-born son of Cūlin, renowned by the name Brahmadatta.
t.1.32.17: I am without a husband, blessings upon you, and I am no one's wife. Since I have approached you in the Brāhma way, you ought to grant me a son.
t.1.32.19: Then that king Brahmadatta dwelt in the city of Kāmpilyā with supreme splendour, just as the king of the gods dwells in heaven.
t.1.32.20: Then, O Kākutstha, that most righteous king Kuśanābha made up his mind to give his hundred daughters to Brahmadatta.
t.1.32.21: Having summoned that Brahmadatta, the greatly radiant king, lord of the earth, gave him his hundred daughters with a heart deeply pleased.
t.1.32.22: Then, O Raghunandana, King Brahmadatta took their hands one by one in due order, like the lord of the gods.
t.1.32.23: Then, the moment their hands were touched, the hundred maidens, no longer hunchbacked and freed from their anguish, shone forth, endowed with supreme beauty.
t.1.32.24: Seeing them released by Vāyu, Kuśanābha, lord of the earth, was supremely delighted and rejoiced again and again.
t.1.32.25: Then the lord of the earth sent off King Brahmadatta, whose marriage had been performed, together with his wives and his company of preceptors.
t.1.32.26: Somadā the Gandharvī, too, greatly delighted at the deed worthy of her son, welcomed those daughters-in-law in accordance with what was proper.
